userStories.title: [CRITICAL] Voice spend (Fish Audio, ElevenLabs) is never estimated or checked against the post or monthly media cap, and its booking can be dropped
userStories.description: D13 and the build prompt's money contract: estimate, then check the post's cap and the workspace's monthly cap, then submit, then book. Footage does this (modules/socials/recipes/footage.py:664-669: priced, one _check_caps over the total, inside the per-workspace footage window). Voice does none of it. modules/socials/recipes/voice.py speak() (:448-489) goes straight from the balance read to FISH_AUDIO_SYNTHESIZE_SPEECH / ELEVENLABS_TEXT_TO_SPEECH, one paid call per line; voice.py never imports media_caps (no check_caps, media_spend or MediaCapExceeded), and its caller modules/socials/render.py _voiced (:312-337) checks nothing either. api/socials.py render_post (:456-509) resolves the voice plan for AVAILABILITY only (voice_recipes.plan_for). So a workspace whose socials.media_monthly_cap_usd is already spent, or set to 0 to forbid paid media, still pays Fish Audio (its API credit is dollars, voice.py:151-152) on every render with a Fish Audio voice, and ElevenLabs characters (the customer's plan) are booked at $0 (voice.py:27, _book :424-445), so no cap ever sees them. An agent reaches it: platform_create_social_post / platform_update_social_post take voice (modules/tools/discovery/actions_socials.py:105) and render by default. Every render re-speaks every line (no reuse, unlike footage slots), so a retry after a failed check pays again. The one booking voice does make is also not durable: _book is called on the event loop (voice.py:483), UsageTracker.track is @off_loop (core/llm/usage_tracker.py:221), so the row is handed to the best-effort threads and returns at once; the next cap check can run before it lands, and when the pool has no free connection within BEST_EFFORT_POOL_WAIT_S (2 s) the write is DROPPED with a warning (core/best_effort.py:55-64): spend without a booking. Footage avoids exactly this with await asyncio.to_thread(_book_rows, ...) (footage.py:643).
acceptanceCriteria: Before the first line is spoken, a toolkit voice render is priced: the script's units (Fish Audio: UTF-8 bytes; ElevenLabs: characters, the recipe's existing units) times a per-toolkit price per unit declared in orchestrator/config.py (no inline literal; add each new name to orchestrator/reports/config-surface.json). The price is checked with media_caps.check_caps against the post's cap and the workspace's monthly cap, inside a per-workspace window shared with footage (the modules/socials/recipes/toolkit.window pattern), so a render's footage and voice are checked against one running total and two renders cannot both spend the same remaining cap. Over either cap, NOTHING is spoken: the render fails with code voice_refused (or the footage refusal's code) and a message naming the cap, what was spent and what the voice would cost; no Composio speech call is made. → DONE — voice.speak prices the script before any call: voice.script_units x recipe.usd_per_unit (Fish Audio UTF-8 bytes x SOCIALS_VOICE_FISH_AUDIO_USD_PER_BYTE 0.000015; ElevenLabs characters x SOCIALS_VOICE_ELEVENLABS_USD_PER_CHARACTER 0.00008; both in config.py and config-surface.json), then media_caps.check_spend (→ check_caps) inside toolkit.spend_window, the per-workspace window footage.generate now takes too (footage's old 'socf' namespace, moved to toolkit.py). Over a cap: VoiceRefused → RenderFailure 'voice_refused', no Composio call. CI run 36455475560 (f4ce18171): test_a_voice_over_the_workspaces_monthly_cap_speaks_nothing_and_books_nothing (message names the monthly cap, $1.00 spent, the voice's $0.0006), test_the_voice_checks_its_caps_inside_the_spend_window_footage_takes and test_footage_prices_and_checks_its_caps_inside_the_spend_window_voice_takes PASSED.

Every voice booking is written before speak() returns and before the window releases: _book runs through await asyncio.to_thread(...) (inline write, as footage.py:643 does), never directly on the event loop. ElevenLabs is booked at its priced amount (units x the configured price), not a hard-coded $0; Fish Audio still books its balance difference and, when the balance after cannot be read, books the priced amount (never $0) with the error recorded. → DONE — voice._speak_lines books with await asyncio.to_thread(_book, ...) inside the credit and spend windows (the tracker writes inline); ElevenLabs books units x the configured price; Fish Audio books its balance difference, or the priced amount with the error recorded when the closing balance cannot be read (voice._cost). userStories.title: [HIGH] Concurrent renders all pass the monthly render quota: it counts only finished renders, so a workspace renders far past its plan's minutes
userStories.description: core/media_render_quota.py enforce_render_quota (:161-170) reads only the seconds already booked on the media lane (render_seconds_used :84-99), and a render books its seconds only when it has finished (modules/socials/render.py:606-611, on the needs_approval path; modules/documents/generation_service.py:651-656, after render_to_file). Nothing reserves the minutes of a render in flight and nothing serializes the check per workspace, so N renders requested before the first one finishes all read the same total and all start. Every render path shares the check: api/socials.py:492 render_post (POST /api/socials/posts/{id}/render and the platform_create_social_post / platform_update_social_post tools, whose render defaults to true) and generation_service.py:626 generate_social (POST /api/documents/generate, the template preview, the generate_document tool, the Playbook generate_document step and the mission coordinator). The design lets ONE render cross the line (media_render_quota.py:24-26); concurrency makes it N. Failure: a Basic workspace (10 minutes) with nothing used requests 20 renders of a 3-minute composition (MEDIA_RENDER_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS 180) within a few seconds, by REST or an agent drafting 20 posts: all 20 pass and up to 60 minutes are rendered and booked, repeatable every time the backlog drains. In normal use, the Weekly social posts Playbook drafts 5 posts that render at once. The render-seconds booking itself is also not durable: book_render_seconds (media_render_quota.py:173-178) is called on the event loop (render.py:611, generation_service.py:651), UsageTracker.track is @off_loop, so the row is written later on the best-effort threads, and it is DROPPED when no pool connection frees within BEST_EFFORT_POOL_WAIT_S (core/best_effort.py:55-64): a dropped row is minutes the quota never counts. The platform already solved this for Auto Live minutes: modules/voice/voice_meter.py counts reserved minutes (MeterReading.committed_minutes = ended_minutes + reserved_minutes).
acceptanceCriteria: A render reserves its seconds (the composition's declared duration) before media-render is called, and the quota compares booked seconds PLUS the seconds reserved by this workspace's renders in flight: a render starts only while booked + reserved < quota. The check and the reservation happen under one per-workspace lock that holds across uvicorn workers (a Postgres advisory lock, the modules/socials/recipes/toolkit.window pattern, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the workspace row). The reservation is released when the render ends: done (replaced by the booked seconds), failed, refused, timed out, or reaped at boot; one that is never released expires with the render's deadline (SOCIALS_RENDER_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS). Both render_post and generate_social use it. No new table unless an existing one cannot hold the reservation (say which in the commit body). → DONE — core/media_render_quota.py: reserve_render holds the composition's declared duration (declared_seconds: ceil of the root data-duration, at most the new SOCIALS_RENDER_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS, 180, which is also the fallback when it cannot be read) as a 'reserved' llm_usage row on the media lane before media-render is called, and a render starts only while booked + reserved < quota. The check and the reservation run in asyncio.to_thread under a per-workspace threading lock, then pg_advisory_xact_lock('rndq', hashtext(workspace)) in a transaction of their own, which holds across the uvicorn workers. Released when the render ends: run_render's finally, after its seconds are booked; render_post's except BaseException for a refusal after the hold; generate_social's finally. One nothing released stops counting after SOCIALS_RENDER_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS plus RESERVATION_GRACE_SECONDS (60), and the boot reaper's new surface deletes it. Both render_post (via render.reserve_seconds) and generate_social use it. No new table: llm_usage holds it, and social_posts could not (generate_document has no post); see commit 3ebc0b04b's body. CI run 36465144154 (25858fb52): test_twenty_renders_asked_at_once_on_basic_start_ten_and_refuse_ten_before_media_render, test_a_render_that_does_not_finish_gives_its_hold_back_and_books_nothing[failed|timed_out|moved_on], test_a_render_that_breaks_unexpectedly_gives_its_hold_back, test_a_render_refused_after_its_hold_gives_it_back, test_a_document_render_that_fails_gives_its_hold_back_and_books_nothing, test_a_hold_nothing_gave_back_stops_counting_at_its_deadline_and_the_boot_reaper_deletes_it, test_a_render_holds_its_declared_duration[*] PASSED.
